symptom: `run --local --watch`: after a Sass error in a theme module is fixed, every following build fails with "[CE6093] The theme could not be compiled" quoting the FIRST error's line, which is no longer in the file; changing to a different error still reports the first; `touch app.mpr` does not help, `mxcli run restart` does. The app keeps serving the last good CSS
cause: mxbuild --serve keeps its first theme compile error as process state and re-reports it as CE6093 (0.3s, no recompile) on every later build in the same process. Not mxcli, not the project: the bundled Dart Sass compiles the generated entry point cleanly at the same moment
insight: Isolated in one harness run against mxbuild 11.12.5's /build API: broken → 'An error occurred while compiling Theme files'; fixed, same process → CE6093 quoting the old error (twice); fresh process → Success. The trigger is 'a theme failure following a theme failure in the same process' — not 'any theme failure' (a first one is genuine and must not cost a 25s restart) and not 'CE6093' alone (it is just the later builds' spelling). A failure that survives the restart is reported from the fresh process and is current, which also fixes 'a different error still reports the first'. The serve restart is shared with #1485's recovery (same class: state in a long-lived mxbuild --serve that only a fresh process clears — see local-loop-silence 'Stale state has more than one home'). Cost the reporter's step list paid: the theme-only fix applies via runtime RESTART, because the fresh build's restartRequired is always true and there is no successful incremental build to take it from. Controls on the same app: pre-fix binary → build #3 failed [CE6093] Undefined variable, served CSS without the fix; fixed → build #3 applied, served CSS has #123456
